text: Writing clean code is an important skill for every programmer. Clean code is easy to read and understand, even for someone who did not write it. One key idea is using clear naming conventions. Choose names that describe what a variable or function does, so others can follow your logic quickly. Another important point is keeping functions small and focused on one task. This makes the code simpler to test and change. Clean code also improves maintainability, because future developers can fix bugs or add features without confusion. In short, readable, well-organized code saves time and helps teams work together more effectively.
